left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1
label: equivalent
why: QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() = 1 against the same window in a derived table filtered on its alias; the order (ts, id) is total, so the kept row is fixed.

left: SELECT user_id, ts, rn FROM (SELECT user_id, ts, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS rn FROM events) WHERE user_id = 1
right: SELECT user_id, ts, rn FROM (SELECT user_id, ts, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS rn FROM events WHERE user_id = 1)
label: equivalent
why: A predicate on the PARTITION BY column keeps or drops whole partitions, so it commutes with the window.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS s FROM events
right: SELECT id, (SELECT SUM(e2.value) FROM events e2 WHERE e2.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM events.user_id) AS s FROM events
label: equivalent
why: A whole-partition windowed SUM is the SUM over the rows with a null-safe equal key (NULL keys form one partition).

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS s FROM events
right: SELECT e.id, g.s FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, SUM(value) AS s FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.user_id
label: equivalent
why: The same windowed SUM against a join to the grouped SUM on a null-safe key.

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id FROM events e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e2 WHERE e2.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM e.user_id AND e2.ts < e.ts)
label: equivalent
why: RANK() = 1 keeps every row tied for the smallest ts, as does NOT EXISTS a smaller ts in the same partition (ts is NOT NULL here).

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) = 1
right: SELECT e.id, e.user_id FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, MIN(ts) AS m FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.user_id AND e.ts = g.m
label: equivalent
why: RANK() = 1 against a join to the grouped MIN: both keep all tied rows.

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e2 WHERE e2.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM e.user_id AND e2.ts < e.ts)
right: SELECT e.id, e.user_id FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, MIN(ts) AS m FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.user_id AND e.ts = g.m
label: equivalent
why: The two window-free 'minimum per group' forms (the one pair of this family the baseline proved).

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: ROW_NUMBER() = 1 keeps one of the rows tied for the smallest ts, RANK() = 1 keeps all of them.

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) = 1
right: SELECT e.id, e.user_id FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, MIN(ts) AS m FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.user_id AND e.ts = g.m
label: not_equivalent
why: The join returns every row tied for the minimum, ROW_NUMBER() = 1 one of them.

left: SELECT user_id, ts, rn FROM (SELECT user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS rn FROM events) WHERE value > 1
right: SELECT user_id, ts, rn FROM (SELECT user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS rn FROM events WHERE value > 1)
label: not_equivalent
why: A predicate on a non-partition column drops rows before the window numbers them, so the row numbers change.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS s FROM events
right: SELECT e.id, g.s FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, SUM(value) AS s FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id = g.user_id
label: not_equivalent
why: A plain = join drops the rows whose user_id is NULL, which the window keeps as one partition.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS s FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS s FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: ROWS stops at the current row, the default RANGE frame includes every peer; they differ when two rows share ts.

left: SELECT id, LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS prev FROM events
right: SELECT id, LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS prev FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: LAG over tied rows takes an arbitrary neighbour; adding id makes it one choice, a subset of the first query's results.

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) <= 2
right: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) <= 2
label: not_equivalent
why: With two rows tied for the smallest ts, RANK skips rank 2 and DENSE_RANK does not; with distinct ts they agree.

left: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: The earliest rows against the latest rows of each user.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1
label: equivalent
why: QUALIFY against a derived table with the same window; the order (ts DESC, id DESC) is total.

left: SELECT user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
right: SELECT user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1
label: equivalent
why: Both sides keep an arbitrary one of the rows tied for the latest ts, so the sets of results are equal although neither is deterministic.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: ROW_NUMBER() = 1 keeps one latest row, RANK() = 1 keeps all of them: the classic latest-row tie trap.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: With id in the order no two rows tie, so ROW_NUMBER() = 1 and RANK() = 1 keep the same row.

left: SELECT e.id, e.user_id, e.ts, e.value FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, MAX(ts) AS m FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id = g.user_id AND e.ts = g.m
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: (user_id, ts) is unique, so the join to the grouped MAX returns one row per user, the row ROW_NUMBER() picks.

left: SELECT e.id, e.user_id, e.ts, e.value FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, MAX(ts) AS m FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id = g.user_id AND e.ts = g.m
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: Without a unique (user_id, ts) the join returns every row tied for the latest ts.

left: SELECT e.id, e.user_id, e.ts, e.value FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, MAX(ts) AS m FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id = g.user_id AND e.ts = g.m
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: Both keep every row tied for the latest ts.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: First event against last event of each user.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: One row per user against one row overall.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) <= 2
label: not_equivalent
why: ROW_NUMBER() = 1 against ROW_NUMBER() <= 2.

left: SELECT user_id, MAX(ts) AS ts FROM events GROUP BY user_id
right: SELECT user_id, ts FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: Only user_id and the ordering column are read, so every tied row looks the same and the result is deterministic.

left: SELECT user_id, ARRAY_AGG(value ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS value FROM events GROUP BY user_id
right: SELECT user_id, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: A total order makes ARRAY_AGG(.. ORDER BY .. LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] the value of the row ROW_NUMBER() = 1 keeps (value is NOT NULL, so the array never holds a NULL). DuckDB cannot run ARRAY_AGG with LIMIT: labelled by reasoning.

left: SELECT user_id, ARRAY_AGG(value ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS value FROM events GROUP BY user_id
right: SELECT user_id, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: Without id in the left order its pick among tied rows is arbitrary, the right query always takes the largest id: the right set of results is a proper subset. Labelled by reasoning (DuckDB cannot run ARRAY_AGG with LIMIT).

left: SELECT user_id, MAX_BY(value, ts) AS value FROM events GROUP BY user_id
right: SELECT user_id, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: MAX_BY(value, ts) takes the value of an arbitrary row tied for the latest ts, as does ROW_NUMBER() = 1 over ORDER BY ts DESC: the sets of results are equal.

left: SELECT user_id, MAX_BY(value, ts) AS value FROM events GROUP BY user_id
right: SELECT user_id, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: MAX_BY is free among tied rows, the right query fixes the largest id: a proper subset of the left set of results.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC) = 1
label: equivalent
why: BigQuery sorts NULL as the smallest value, so DESC puts it last by default.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC NULLS FIRST, id DESC) = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: A NULL ts is the latest row of its user under NULLS FIRST and the earliest by default.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1 AND user_id = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events WHERE user_id = 1) WHERE rn = 1
label: equivalent
why: A filter on the partition column commutes with the window.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1 AND ts > 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events WHERE ts > 1) WHERE rn = 1
label: equivalent
why: The latest row has the largest ts, so a lower bound on ts keeps it or drops the whole user, and filtering first picks the same row among the survivors.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn = 1 AND ts < 3
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM events WHERE ts < 3) WHERE rn = 1
label: not_equivalent
why: An upper bound on ts drops the latest row of a user; filtering first makes the next row the latest.

left: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events WHERE value > 1 QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1
right: SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM (SELECT id, user_id, ts, value FROM events QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) = 1) WHERE value > 1
label: not_equivalent
why: QUALIFY runs after WHERE: the left query takes the latest row among the rows with value > 1, the right one drops the user whose latest row has value <= 1.

left: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
right: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_id FROM flagged
label: equivalent
why: A running SUM over a total order: the default RANGE frame and ROWS agree because no two rows are peers.

left: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) > 1 OR value <> LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts), 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS session_id FROM flagged
right: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) > 1 OR value <> LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id), 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
label: not_equivalent
why: A session also ends when the event kind (value) changes; between tied events the LAG neighbour, hence the flags, depend on the tie order, and the right query fixes one order.

left: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS session_id FROM flagged
right: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
label: equivalent
why: Only ts feeds the flags: tied events share ts, so the second of two tied events never opens a session, and the default frame gives every peer the same total. Which tied event comes first does not show.

left: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS session_id FROM flagged
right: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_id FROM flagged
label: equivalent
why: (user_id, ts) is unique, so ROWS and the default frame cover the same rows and LAG has one answer.

left: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
right: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) >= 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
label: not_equivalent
why: A gap of exactly 1 starts a new session in one query only.

left: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
right: WITH flagged AS (SELECT id, user_id, ts, IF(LAG(ts) OVER ( ORDER BY ts, id) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER ( ORDER BY ts, id) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events) SELECT id, user_id, ts, SUM(is_new) OVER ( ORDER BY ts, id) AS session_id FROM flagged
label: not_equivalent
why: Sessions counted over all users against per user.

left: SELECT id, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events
right: SELECT id, IF(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events p WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.ts < e.ts AND p.ts >= e.ts - 1), 0, 1) AS is_new FROM events e
label: equivalent
why: With unique (user_id, ts) the previous event is the latest earlier one, and a gap above 1 means none within 1.

left: SELECT id, IF(LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) IS NULL OR ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) > 1, 1, 0) AS is_new FROM events
right: SELECT id, IF(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events p WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.ts < e.ts AND p.ts >= e.ts - 1), 0, 1) AS is_new FROM events e
label: not_equivalent
why: Two events with the same earliest ts: LAG gives the first of them no predecessor and the second a gap of 0 and so no new session, NOT EXISTS flags both as new.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
label: equivalent
why: No two rows are peers under (ts, id), so RANGE and ROWS frames hold the same rows.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS total FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: Rows tied on ts are peers of the default frame, so they share one total; under ROWS each gets its own, in an arbitrary order.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
label: equivalent
why: The default frame with an ORDER BY is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS total FROM events
label: equivalent
why: (user_id, ts) is unique, so ROWS and RANGE agree.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT e.id, SUM(p.value) AS total FROM events e JOIN events p ON p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.ts <= e.ts GROUP BY e.id
label: equivalent
why: The default RANGE frame is the sum over every row of the user with ts <= the current ts, as the self-join computes (id is unique, so GROUP BY e.id keeps each row once).

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT e.id, SUM(p.value) AS total FROM events e JOIN events p ON p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.ts <= e.ts GROUP BY e.id
label: not_equivalent
why: The self-join sums every tied row; the ROWS frame only the ones ordered before the current row.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT e.id, SUM(p.value) AS total FROM events e JOIN events p ON p.user_id = e.user_id AND (p.ts < e.ts OR (p.ts = e.ts AND p.id <= e.id)) GROUP BY e.id
label: equivalent
why: ROWS over the total order (ts, id) sums the rows that sort at or before the current one.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER ( ORDER BY ts, id) AS total FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: A running total per user against one over all users.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS total FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: Totals from the first event against totals from the last.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT e.id, g.total FROM events e JOIN (SELECT user_id, SUM(value) AS total FROM events GROUP BY user_id) g ON e.user_id = g.user_id
label: equivalent
why: user_id is NOT NULL here, so a plain = join matches the partitions.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS total FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: The partition total against the running total.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id ROWS 2 PRECEDING) AS total FROM events
label: equivalent
why: ROWS 2 PRECEDING is the shorthand for ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.

left: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
right: SELECT id, SUM(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS total FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: Which two earlier rows a ROWS frame holds depends on how tied rows are ordered.

left: SELECT id, value FROM (SELECT id, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS rn FROM events)
right: SELECT id, value FROM events
label: equivalent
why: A window nothing reads cannot change the rows, even though its order has ties.

left: SELECT id, value FROM (SELECT id, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ts, id) AS rn FROM events) WHERE rn <= 2
right: SELECT id, value FROM events
label: not_equivalent
why: Keeping the first two rows against keeping all rows.

left: SELECT id, LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS other FROM events
right: SELECT id, LEAD(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, id DESC) AS other FROM events
label: equivalent
why: The previous row in ascending (ts, id) order is the next row in descending order.

left: SELECT id, LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS other FROM events
right: SELECT id, LAG(value) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts, id) AS other FROM events
label: not_equivalent
